label: Deemed supply on closure: deduction rate per taxable period, non-building depreciable assets
unit: % of acquisition cost deducted per elapsed taxable period
appliesTo: Machinery, equipment, fixtures, vehicles and other non-building depreciable assets held at closure, where input VAT was deducted on purchase
why: Because the widespread shortcut — 'value the leftovers at market price, or at book value' — is wrong for exactly the assets worth the most money. Ordinary stock is valued at market value; depreciable assets have their own statutory formula, and it is neither market value nor the depreciated figure in the accounts. Getting this wrong produces a final VAT bill that is too high as often as too low.

history.display: 25% per taxable period, capped at 4 periods
history.source: Enforcement Decree of the Value-Added Tax Act, art. 66
history.note: Supply value = acquisition cost × [1 − 25% × elapsed taxable periods], counting a maximum of four periods. Korean VAT taxable periods are half-yearly, so four periods is roughly two years: an asset bought more than two years before closure reaches zero and carries no deemed-supply VAT, while one bought shortly before closure is taxed on most of its cost. This only applies where input VAT was deducted at purchase.
